html:
The Meskwaki, called the Fox by the French, are an Algonquian people of the western Great Lakes. Their name means "red earth people". The 1492 map puts them in what is now southern Michigan, matching accounts that they lived there before the wars of the 1600s, such as the Beaver Wars, pushed them west.

By the later 1600s they lived in Wisconsin, around the Fox River, which is named after them. They controlled the Fox and Wisconsin rivers, the canoe route between the Great Lakes and the Mississippi, and charged French traders for passage. This led to the Fox Wars of 1712 to 1733, in which the French and their allies killed most of the Meskwaki. The survivors joined the closely related Sauk, and the two peoples have been allies ever since; see Sauk and Meskwaki.

In 1857 a group bought land on the Iowa River, the Meskwaki Settlement, which they still own. Others belong to the Sac and Fox Nation in Oklahoma and Kansas. See also Fox.
